subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 4: Globalisation and the Indian Economy
central_question: How have MNCs, foreign trade, technology and liberalisation integrated India with the world economy, and why have the benefits and costs been uneven?
in_scope_units: Production Across Countries: the spread of MNC production
Interlinking Production Across Countries: foreign investment, partnerships, acquisitions and supply orders
Foreign Trade and Integration of Markets
What Is Globalisation?: rapid integration through trade and investment
Factors That Have Enabled Globalisation: transport and information technology
Liberalisation of Foreign Trade and Foreign Investment Policy
World Trade Organisation and the debate on fair trade practices
Impact of Globalisation in India: consumers, MNCs, Indian firms and service exports
The Struggle for a Fair Globalisation
banned_topics: GDP, disguised unemployment and sector classification

known_pitfalls.claim: An MNC is any company that exports goods.
known_pitfalls.correction: An MNC owns or controls production in more than one nation.

known_pitfalls.claim: Foreign trade and foreign investment are the same.
known_pitfalls.correction: Foreign trade is cross-border buying and selling; foreign investment is spending on productive assets in another country.

known_pitfalls.claim: Liberalisation means government has no role.
known_pitfalls.correction: Liberalisation means reducing trade and investment restrictions; government still regulates, supports and negotiates.

known_pitfalls.claim: Globalisation benefits all producers and workers equally.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter shows gains for some groups and losses or insecurity for many small producers and workers.

recommended_example_progression: Use the NCERT industrial-equipment MNC example to map a global production chain.
Use the NCERT Cargill–Parakh and Ford Motors cases to explain foreign investment and interlinking.
Use the NCERT Chinese-toys example to analyse market integration and unequal effects.
Use the NCERT London-magazine example for IT-enabled globalisation.
Use the NCERT Sushila garment-worker case to evaluate fair globalisation.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with 'EXERCISES', Questions 1–13, followed by an Additional Activity / Project.
